nodes.name: Lusztig's reduction to graded affine Hecke algebras
nodes.statement: Lusztig \cite{Lu1} proved that certain module category of an affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some graded affine Hecke algebra.
conclusions: certain module category of an affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some graded affine Hecke algebra

nodes.name: Lascoux-Leclerc-Thibon conjecture
nodes.statement: In order to compute the decomposition numbers of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of type $A$ at an $e$th root of unity over $\mathbb{C}$, Lascoux, Leclerc, and Thibon \cite{LLT} suggested the conjecture that the decomposition numbers can be computed using the canonical bases of quantum groups of affine type $A.$
assumptions: the Iwahori-Hecke algebra of type $A$ at an $e$th root of unity over $\mathbb{C}$
conclusions: the decomposition numbers can be computed using the canonical bases of quantum groups of affine type $A.$

nodes.name: Ariki's theorem
nodes.statement: Later on, using the geometric results of Kazhdan-Lusztig and Ginzburg, Ariki \cite{Ari} proved this conjecture by establishing a connection between the representation theory of cyclotomic Hecke algebras and the canonical bases of integrable highest weight modules over $\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_{e}(\mathbb{C}).$
conclusions: Ariki \cite{Ari} proved this conjecture

nodes.name: Khovanov-Lauda-Rouquier categorification theorem
nodes.statement: In order to provide a categorification of quantum groups, Khovanov and Lauda \cite{KhLa1, KhLa2} and Rouquier \cite{Rou1} have independently introduced a new family of algebras associated to a generalized Cartan matrix, known as quiver Hecke algebras or Khovanov-Lauda-Rouquier algebras. Moreover, they have shown that there exists an algebra isomorphism between the integral form of the negative half of a quantum group and the Grothendieck group of the additive category of finitely generated graded projective modules of a quiver Hecke algebra.
conclusions: there exists an algebra isomorphism between the integral form of the negative half of a quantum group and the Grothendieck group of the additive category of finitely generated graded projective modules of a quiver Hecke algebra

nodes.name: Varagnolo-Vasserot-Rouquier canonical basis theorem
nodes.statement: Later on, when the Cartan matrix is symmetric, Varagnolo and Vasserot \cite{VV} and independently Rouquier \cite{Rou2} proved that Lusztig's canonical bases or Kashiwara's lower global bases correspond to the isomorphism classes of graded self-dual indecomposable projective modules under this isomorphism.
assumptions: when the Cartan matrix is symmetric
conclusions: Lusztig's canonical bases or Kashiwara's lower global bases correspond to the isomorphism classes of graded self-dual indecomposable projective modules under this isomorphism

nodes.name: Rouquier's categorical equivalence theorem
nodes.statement: Rouquier \cite{Rou1} also proved that certain module category of an affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some quiver Hecke algebra of (affine) type $A$.
conclusions: certain module category of an affine and degenerate affine Hecke algebra is equivalent to its suitable counterpart of some quiver Hecke algebra of (affine) type $A$

nodes.name: Yokonuma-Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: The Yokonuma-Hecke algebra $Y_{r,n}(q)$ (of type $A$) is a quotient of the group algebra of the modular framed braid group $(\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\wr B_{n},$ where $B_{n}$ is the braid group on $n$ strands (of type $A$).
nodes.genus: a quotient of the group algebra of the modular framed braid group $(\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})\wr B_{n},$

nodes.name: Rostam's theorem
nodes.statement: Recently, Rostam \cite{Ro} has shown that cyclotomic Yokonuma-Hecke algebras are particular cases of cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras, generalizing the results of Brundan and Kleshchev.
conclusions: cyclotomic Yokonuma-Hecke algebras are particular cases of cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras

nodes.name: base field $k$ and root of unity $\zeta$
nodes.statement: Let $r, n\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1},$ and let $k$ be a field which contains a primitive $r$th root of unity $\zeta.$

nodes.name: quantum characteristic $e$
nodes.statement: We denote by $e$ the smallest integer such that $1+q+\cdots+q^{e-1}=0$, and set $e:=\infty$ if no such integer exists.

nodes.statement: Assume now that $q\neq 1.$ Given a subset $I$ of $k^{*},$ we denote by $I_{q}$ the quiver with set of vertices $I$ and with an arrow $i\rightarrow qi$ whenever $i, qi\in I.$

nodes.name: types of the quiver $I_q$
nodes.statement: Note that when $q=1,$ $I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< p$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $p=0;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $p=0;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{p-1}$ if $|I|=p> 0.$ When $q\neq 1,$ $I_{q}$ has type $A_{\ell}$ if $\vert I\vert=\ell< e$ or $|I|=\ell$ and $e=\infty;$ type $A_{\infty}$ if $|I|=\infty$ and $e=\infty;$ type $\widetilde{A}_{e-1}$ if $|I|=e> 0.$
nodes.statement_short: $I_q$ is of type $A_\ell$, $A_\infty$ or affine $\widetilde{A}$ depending on $|I|$ and on $p$ (if $q=1$) or $e$ (if $q\neq1$).

nodes.name: quiver $\Gamma$
nodes.statement: We now define the quiver $\Gamma=\coprod_{j\in J} I_{q},$ which is $r$ disjoint copies of $I_{q}.$

nodes.name: coefficient ring $\mathcal{R}$
nodes.statement: Let $q$ be an indeterminate and let $\mathcal{R}=\mathbb{Z}[\frac{1}{r}][q,q^{-1}].$

nodes.name: affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra
nodes.statement:
The affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra, denoted by $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(q)$, is an $\mathcal{R}$-associative algebra generated by the elements $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},\ldots,g_{n-1},X_{1}^{\pm1},$ in which the generators $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},$ $\ldots,g_{n-1}$ satisfy the following relations:
\begin{align}
g_ig_j&=g_jg_i \qquad \qquad\qquad\quad\hspace{0.3cm}\mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n-1$ such that $\vert i-j\vert \geq 2$;} \\[0.1em]
g_ig_{i+1}g_i&=g_{i+1}g_ig_{i+1} \qquad \quad\qquad\hspace{0.05cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-2$;} \\[0.1em]
t_it_j&=t_jt_i \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad  \mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em]
g_it_j&=t_{s_i(j)}g_i \quad \quad\qquad\qquad\hspace{0.25cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$ and $j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em]
t_i^r&=1 \quad \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.2em]
g_{i}^{2}&=q+(q-1)e_{i}g_{i} \qquad \hspace{0.48cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$;} \end{align}
where $s_{i}$ is the transposition $(i,i+1)$, and for each $1\leq i\leq n-1$,
$$e_{i} :=\frac{1}{r}\sum\limits_{s=0}^{r-1}t_{i}^{s}t_{i+1}^{-s},$$
together with the following relations concerning the generators $X_{1}^{\pm1}$:
\begin{align}
X_{1}X_{1}^{-1}&=X_{1}^{-1}X_{1}=1; \\[0.1em]
g_{1}X_{1}g_{1}X_{1}&=X_{1}g_{1}X_{1}g_{1}; \\[0.1em]
g_{i}X_{1}&=X_{1}g_{i} \qquad \qquad \quad\mbox{for all $i=2,\ldots,n-1$;} \\[0.1em]
t_{j}X_{1}&=X_{1}t_{j} \qquad \qquad\quad\mbox{for all $j=1,\ldots,n$;} \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(q)$: generators $t_i$, $g_i$, $X_1^{\pm1}$ with braid, framing, $t_i^r=1$, quadratic $g_i^2=q+(q-1)e_ig_i$ and affine relations.

nodes.name: degenerate affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra
nodes.statement:
The degenerate affine Yokonuma-Hecke algebra, denoted by $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(1)$, is an $\mathcal{R}$-associative algebra generated by the elements $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},f_{1},\ldots,f_{n-1},y_1,\ldots, y_{n}$ in which the generators $t_{1},\ldots,t_{n},g_{1},$ $\ldots,g_{n-1}$ satisfy the following relations:
\begin{align}
f_if_j&=f_jf_i \qquad \qquad\qquad\quad\hspace{0.3cm}\mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n-1$ such that $\vert i-j\vert \geq 2$;} \\[0.1em]
f_if_{i+1}f_i&=f_{i+1}f_if_{i+1} \qquad \quad\qquad\hspace{0.05cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-2$;} \\[0.1em]
t_it_j&=t_jt_i \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad  \mbox{for all $i,j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em]
f_it_j&=t_{s_i(j)}f_i \quad \quad\qquad\qquad\hspace{0.25cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$ and $j=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.1em]
t_i^r&=1 \quad \qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n$;} \\[0.2em]
f_{i}^{2}&=1 \qquad \hspace{2.71cm}\mbox{for all $i=1,\ldots,n-1$;} \end{align}
together with the following relations concerning the generators $y_1,\ldots, y_{n}$:
\begin{align}
y_{i}y_{j}&=y_{j}y_{i}; \\[0.1em]
f_{i}y_{i+1}&=y_{i}f_{i}+e_{i}; \\[0.1em]
f_{i}y_{j}&=y_{j}f_{i} \qquad \qquad \quad\mbox{for all $j\neq i, i+1$;} \\[0.1em]
t_{j}y_{i}&=y_{i}t_{j} \hspace{0.07cm}\qquad \qquad\quad\mbox{for all $i, j=1,\ldots,n$;} \end{align}
where for each $1\leq i\leq n-1$,
$$e_{i} :=\frac{1}{r}\sum\limits_{s=0}^{r-1}t_{i}^{s}t_{i+1}^{-s}.$$
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat{Y}_{r,n}(1)$: generators $t_i$, $f_i$, $y_i$ with symmetric-group, framing and degenerate affine relations $f_iy_{i+1}=y_if_i+e_i$.
